label: In every possible history, each moment with a contingent concrete thing present has a begun past
paraphrase: OPEN analyst premise, attribution deferred: in every history accessible from the selected world, every moment at which some contingent concrete individual is present has a past with a beginning (some moment at or before it has no earlier moment). It denies the begun version of horn H2 (a beginningless past at a populated moment) wherever a contingent concrete thing is present; histories with no contingent concrete thing present are unconstrained. Unlike founded populated pasts it allows continuous time with a first moment. Its cost: it excludes, in every accessible history, contingent presence in a past with no first moment even when that past is metrically finite. Standard FLRW Big Bang cosmology has such a past (time open below; the initial singularity is not a moment), so this premise denies that such a cosmology, populated, is possible. Because the beginning is a first moment of the shared time order, not of events, it also excludes empty beginningless time before a first event (creation in an absolute time with no first moment). In a branching order one minimal moment at or below a populated moment suffices, so other branches below it may be beginningless. It mentions no cause. 'Concrete' is the supplied Concrete parameter.
